source.title: First-in-Human Adjunctive Bacteriophage Therapy for Malakoplakia
source.authors: Saima Aslam; Aleah Brubaker; Mita Shah; Thomas C. S. Martin; Tyler Mandt; Austin-Marley Windham-Herman; Haiyan Zhang; Tina Bryde; Yilmaz Emre Gencay; Aurelie Gram; Christian Grøndahl; Jakob Krause Haaber; Björn Hallström; Eric van der Helm; Jonas Hink; Lorrie Maccario; Anders Østergaard; Alice Troy; Niloofar Yavari; Robert T. Schooley; Sanjay Mehta
source.source_material_scope: Primary article only; no correction or supplementary source material supplied for this task.

atoms.canonical_statement: The report describes the first human use of adjunctive bacteriophage therapy for Escherichia coli-related malakoplakia in a kidney transplant recipient.
The patient was a 65-year-old man with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis who received a deceased-donor kidney transplant in February 2023 and subsequently developed progressive malakoplakia.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

atoms.canonical_statement: Post-transplant disease included recurrent E. coli bacteremia and urinary tract infections, necrotizing graft pyelonephritis, chronic prostatitis, urine leak, and a progressive bladder/prostate-associated mass with cutaneous extension; biopsy confirmed malakoplakia with Michaelis-Gutmann bodies.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

atoms.canonical_statement: The patient’s E. coli isolate was resistant to quinolones, cephalosporins, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and later became carbapenem-resistant during progressive disease.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

atoms.canonical_statement: SNIPR001 was a cocktail of four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems designed to induce DNA breaks in essential bacterial genes.

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Against the patient’s E. coli isolate, SNIPR001 had a measured titer of 7.4 × 10^10 PFU/mL.

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

concept.text: SNIPR001 titer against the clinical isolate

atoms.canonical_statement: Intravenous SNIPR001 was administered as 2 mL of 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL twice daily for 2 weeks as a slow IV push over 1 minute with saline flushes before and after each dose.

exposures.details: 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL; slow IV push over 1 minute with 10 mL normal saline flush before and after dose

atoms.canonical_statement: Topical SNIPR001 was administered as 2 mL of 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL twice daily and continued until the abdominal wall lesions healed.

exposures.details: 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL poured over visible lesions and allowed to absorb 15–30 minutes

atoms.canonical_statement: Intralesional SNIPR001 was administered as 6 mL of 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL into the intra-abdominal mass under ultrasound guidance once weekly for 8 weeks.

exposures.details: 1 × 10^9 PFU/mL; injected at multiple locations under ultrasound guidance

atoms.canonical_statement: At SNIPR001 initiation, the patient was receiving tigecycline and either meropenem or fosfomycin; high-dose ascorbic acid and bethanechol had been started 11 days earlier, and phage therapy was added to this existing regimen.

exposures.details: Tigecycline plus meropenem or fosfomycin; high-dose ascorbic acid and bethanechol

atoms.canonical_statement: The patient tolerated intravenous, topical, and intralesional SNIPR001 without phage-related adverse events.

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Pancytopenia developed before SNIPR001 while the patient was receiving high-dose meropenem and tigecycline, worsened after phage initiation, and resolved after meropenem was discontinued.

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Within 1 week of SNIPR001 initiation, the abdominal cutaneous lesions improved markedly, with several lesions fully healed by 4 weeks.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: The intra-abdominal malakoplakia mass decreased from 744.6 cm³ at baseline to 373.4 cm³ at week 8, reported as a 50% reduction.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: The intra-abdominal malakoplakia mass measured 82 cm³ at 1 year, reported as an 89% reduction from the 744.6 cm³ baseline.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: The urine leak resolved without surgical intervention after adjunctive phage therapy was initiated.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Urine culture at 88 days and tissue culture from the intra-abdominal mass at 161 days after phage initiation were negative.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: No growth of E. coli was observed in post-phage cultures during the reported treatment course.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: No serum phage neutralization was detected through week 8 of SNIPR001 therapy.

population.label: 65-year-old male deceased-donor kidney transplant recipient with progressive E. coli-related malakoplakia

exposures.details: Four engineered bacteriophages carrying CRISPR-Cas systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Because this was a single-patient experience with concurrent antibiotic and adjunctive treatments, causal attribution of clinical improvement to phage therapy alone cannot be established.
Long-term durability of remission and the risk of recurrence remain unknown.
Absence of phage neutralization in this case may not generalize because intravenous exposure was limited to 2 weeks and patient-specific or phage-specific immune factors may have contributed.
The authors conclude that adjunctive phage therapy was feasible and tolerated alongside standard-of-care systemic antibiotics in this immunosuppressed patient with progressive malakoplakia.
Whole-genome sequencing data for E. coli isolate b9106 were deposited in the Sequence Read Archive under BioProject PRJNA1338204.
The clinical work received no external funding; SNIPR001 was provided free of cost by SNIPR Biome, while CARB-X and other funders supported development of SNIPR001.
Multiple authors reported employment, founder, advisory-board, or consultant relationships with SNIPR Biome or other phage-related companies.
